## Playa Esmeralda — Cuba's "Emerald Coast"!

Playa Esmeralda is a very popular holiday destination near Naranjo Bay in Holguín Province. The beach is located 5 km from the town of Guardalavaca. It is considered Cuba's most picturesque beach. Its name means "emerald coast," a fitting description of the scene.

## Playa Esmeralda — a beach paradise!

At Playa Esmeralda, the sand is as white as powdered sugar, the water is crystal clear, and beautiful offshore reefs teem with extraordinary marine life. Visitors can enjoy almost every kind of water sport: deep-water diving, fishing, windsurfing, sailing, pedal boating and snorkeling, as well as relaxing on the beach. Cuba's highest mountain peak is also described as being in this area, whose natural landscapes are exceptionally rich and diverse. Playa Esmeralda is described as having more than a hundred beaches, numerous caves, rivers, mountains, waterfalls and natural springs.

## Surfing, diving and nightlife: things to do in Tamarindo, Costa Rica

This upscale beach resort is a 45-minute flight from San José. Tamarindo Beach (Playa Tamarindo) stretches for more than 3.5 km and has been awarded Blue Flag recognition for the environmental condition of its beach and surroundings.

Tamarindo is equally well suited to a relaxing holiday and a surfing trip. Activities include sport fishing, sailing, diving and snorkeling, golf, canopy tours and boat trips through the jungle.

## Activities in Tamarindo

Tamarindo combines a relaxed holiday atmosphere with excellent conditions for surfers. There are numerous restaurants serving cuisines from around the world, as well as casinos, art galleries, craft shops selling pottery, shopping centers and nightclubs.

This seaside resort lies on a small peninsula 75 km south of Dangriga. It is known for a scenic lagoon bordered by 5 km of sandy beaches, considered among the finest in Belize.

Placencia's beachfront promenade is reputed to be the narrowest promenade in the world. Numerous bars, restaurants and shops line the walkway.

Placencia offers windsurfing, thanks to the steady northeasterly winds that blow across the sea around the peninsula. Diving equipment can be rented from hotels. Boats depart from Placencia for the Barrier Reef, which stretches for 320 km along Belize's coast and is the world's second-largest coral reef.

Playa Blanca is located on Bolivia's Uyuni Salt Flat. On routes across the salt plain, it is known as the Salt Museum: the former building of a salt hotel has become a stop where visitors learn how salt is used in construction.

Here, salt is interesting as a material for walls and interior objects. A visit helps connect what travelers see in Colchani, where salt is extracted and processed, with the architecture found on the salt flat.

The museum features on some day routes between Colchani and Incahuasi Island. Visits, transport and stops on the salt flat depend on the itinerary selected; overnight accommodation is booked separately at the specified hotel.

Playa Blanca is a beach resort on Panama's Pacific coast. It is a place to spend a few relaxing days beside the ocean after traveling through the countries of Central America.

The main activity here is simply enjoying the coast. Beach days are left free, so you can spend your time walking along the shore and swimming, while choosing any additional activities independently.

The resort is associated with the Playa Blanca Beach Resort hotel, mentioned in the tour itinerary. A beach stay can be combined with visits to Panama City and other parts of Panama.
